name: Template — create / edit form
$fence: EXAMPLE, NOT A PART. However we probably need to create some standardised templates for some programs. So: this page is properly composed of parts (s313-D72) AND fenced — the compose door (_compose_slice.py load_graph) skips it, the generate-from-canon skill never starts from it, and _validate_example_fence.py refuses a build that reads or traces it.
purpose: The page a person fills in to CREATE a new record, and the same page re-entered to EDIT an existing one. It is an organism-of-organisms: an app bar, a page-head lock-up, a form column beside a guidance aside, and an action bar that stays reachable. It contributes page-scale LAYOUT and nothing else - every control inside it is a gated component, borrowed.

props.name: mode
props.$note: CREATE starts empty and its action bar is Cancel + Save. EDIT arrives prefilled, gains an unsaved-changes strip on first edit, gains a destructive action pushed to the far edge, and may lock fields whose change is a different journey. Both are drawn in the snippet.

props.name: guidance
props.$note: Whether the guidance aside is present. When absent the form column takes the full width; when present it is 320px and moves BELOW the form at container <=880px.

props.name: destructiveAction
props.$note: EDIT only. Rendered with .fl-spacer so it sits at the opposite edge from Save and is never adjacent to it.

props.name: stickyActions
props.$note: The action bar is position:sticky against the nearest SCROLLPORT. On a real page that is the page. See the antiPattern about reference pages.

props.name: title
props.$note: The page's title, which says whether the record is being created or edited. s305-D17 (Dave, #305 call 16, "yes"): a part's own words are a field on the part, not a separate text part inside it, so the gate checks them with the part (length, wrap, the 44px target, the name a screen reader hears). Added #311 lane C0.

variants.name: create
variants.use: A new record. Empty fields, no destructive action, no dirty state.

variants.name: edit
variants.use: An existing record. Prefilled, dirty-state strip, destructive action, optionally locked fields.

tokens.divider: divider/border/section - the page's own section rules
tokens.focus: focus/ring - read only by the demo bar
tokens.$parts: Every other colour, radius, size and face on the page belongs to a part and is bound in THAT part's #token-manifest; the page binds nothing for them (s307-D75: the rules live in the shared stylesheet, not on the page).
tokens.$mono: MONO base rendered; the other themes reach the page through canon.css's theme cascade on each part's scope.
tokens.$noNewWidths: s210-D3 discipline: the template declares viewport-level layout (a 320px aside track and a 2-column grid). No molecule inside it receives a new fixed width - the form column keeps Form-layout's own max-width:420px.

livesInside: Modal or drawer, when the record is small

$composes-note: REBUILT #314 lane TP (s313-D72, Dave's comment verbatim: "We need to regenerate the templates too BTW, everything in the library should be a valid 'element' of the design system"). The template is a composed PAGE: its snippet links canon/canon.css and places each part above as its own .cn-<slug> scope with the part's own markup; the page's <style> carries placement rules only (s305-D57 rule 3a; s307-D75). Before #314 it carried copies of the parts' rules and canon.css projected that second copy under its own scope. The #210 prose that stood here (which classes were copied, declaration for declaration) is retired with the copies. FIX ROUND #314 TP: Cancel is a quaternary Button in the Action-bar's slot; the third specimen, Form-layout's own validation vocabulary (is-error, is-ok), is back; the lede is page prose under the lock-up.

accessibility.roles: No invented roles. The app bar is a <header>, the page body a <main>, the guidance panel an <aside> with aria-labelledby, the form-level error box role="alert" with tabindex=-1 so focus can land on it.
accessibility.keyboard: Tab order follows source order: app bar, page head, form fields, guidance aside, action bar. Every error-summary entry is a real link that moves focus to its field. The (?) help control is a real <button> with an accessible name.
accessibility.announcements: Each field message is an aria-live=polite region. The unsaved-changes strip announces once, on the first real change, via a visually-hidden live region - not on every keystroke.
accessibility.states: aria-invalid is set and cleared per field; disabled fields carry the real disabled attribute so AT reports them, and the reason sits in the field's help text rather than only in the visual dimming.
accessibility.targets: Every action-bar button is 44px tall. The (?) help control is 18px with the canon aid-009 ::before hit expander to 44.
accessibility.$colourIsNeverAlone: The error channel is border + a 4px stroke + a roundel + ink message text (1.4.1). The unsaved-changes strip is ink on a hover-wash with the word 'Unsaved' carrying the meaning - deliberately NOT the warning seat.
accessibility.$knownDelta: Form-layout bumps an errored or completed input to font-weight:500. That bump is ABSENT here because the canon type ramp has no 16/500 INPUT composite and a raw font-weight declaration would breach the shrink-only type ratchet. The error channel is unharmed but the WEIGHT cue is gone. Named for Dave, not smoothed over.

antiPatterns: Re-drawing a field. Every input in this template is Form-layout's boxed-field anatomy with its class names intact. If the field language needs to change, change it in Input-fields and let Form-layout follow - never fork it here.
Putting the destructive action next to Save. It is placed with .fl-spacer at the opposite edge on purpose.

Treating a locked field as merely dimmed. A field the user may not change must say WHY in its help text; dimming alone is a dead end (the #209 cancelled-mandate lesson: disabled ink is exempt from 1.4.3 and can become unreadable).

Assuming position:sticky sticks to the template. It sticks to the nearest SCROLLPORT. MEASURED at #210 on a reference page holding two templates: the bar painted over its own live fields (bar 1594-1671 across a form running 1562-2027). If a template is not the page, give it a scrollport.
Growing the guidance aside into a second form. It is read-only guidance; a control in there competes with the form for the same decision.
REVIEW Adding a RAG hue to the unsaved-changes strip. It is currently ink-only. Whether an unsaved state is a WARNING is Dave's call and touches the two-red law.

Copying a part's rules onto the page. The page places parts (its own .cn-<slug> scope + the part's own markup) and never resizes or restyles them (s305-D57 rule 3a, s307-D75). A template that re-declares a Button ladder, a Summary row or a Data-grid toolbar forks the part the moment the part moves.
